description: IndexedZSet<K,V> cross-language conformance — the rung ABOVE the Z-set on the algebra ladder (G-Set ⊂ Bag ⊂ Z-set ⊂ IndexedZSet). An IndexedZSet is conceptually Z[K × V] (a Z-set over (key, value) pairs) but stored GROUPED BY KEY: an ascending-by-key run of groups, each carrying its per-key Z-set<V>. That grouping is what turns the bilinear JOIN and key-wise aggregation into a linear merge over two sorted runs — which is why it is the substrate DBSP incremental views are built on. Mirrors the F# engine src/Core/IndexedZSet.fs (the originating oracle). Canonical form (the equality contract for cross-oracle byte-diff): groups sorted ascending by key (no key twice), each group's values a canonical Z-set (sorted by value, weight != 0), and a group whose values cancel to empty is DROPPED (the abelian-group inverse lifts to the indexed level). Every op reduces to the Z-set primitive: indexWith buckets-by-key then Z-set-canonicalizes each bucket (sum + drop-zero); add merge-joins the runs and ZSet.unions shared keys; neg negates per group; sub = add(a, neg(b)); join merge-joins on key then cross-products the value-Z-sets with weight-MULTIPLY + consolidate. The fixture is intentionally small + hand-verifiable: build A via indexWith(indexInput) and assert == expectedA, then assert add/neg/sub/join/toZSet of A against operandB.
comparator: ascending ordinal on the key, then ascending ordinal on the value (TS string < / C# StringComparer.Ordinal / byte-ordered Rust Ord). Same ASCII-only caveat as the Z-set/Bag oracles: F# Comparer<'K>.Default is culture-sensitive but coincides with ordinal for these single-letter keys/values.

combiners.toZSet: (k, v) => `${k}|${v}` — flatten a (key,value) tuple to a single string element
combiners.join: (k, va, vb) => `${k}|${va}|${vb}` — name a joined triple as a single string element

indexInput.note: second (a,x) — sums with the first to weight 2

expectedAddAB.note: key a: union({x:2,y:2},{x:-2,z:1}) → x cancels to 0 (DROPPED), y:2, z:1

expectedSubAB.note: add(A, neg(B)): key a union({x:2,y:2},{x:2,z:-1}) → x:4, y:2, z:-1 (negative persists)
